items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: I mean you know ask James Brown. I mean that comes, that’s a fact in a lot of music.

ctx.x: I love what you’re saying about this. And it makes me think about rhythm sections and what they do with the time. And I’m wondering, in your opinion, in the Cookers, who’s the main, who’s in the driver’s seat as far as the rhythm or is it a shared responsibility? And the reason I ask this is Cecil McBee said some very eloquent things about quarter notes, about playing the bass and approaching the quarter notes. And he said to the bassists, you are the timekeeper. You are the vibe of the entire group.

That’s true. I agree with that. I mean you know ask James Brown. I mean that comes, that’s a fact in a lot of music. The drummer seemingly is the guy, because he’s a little more easy to focus on him, plus with the fills and everything there’s more going on with the drummer. But the drummer can’t do that without the foundation from a bass player. And I have found, interestingly, and this is not, I mean you mentioned Cecil but this has got nothing to do with Cecil. What I have found over the years talking to…

guy was just [hand motion straight ahead] you know because they wanted that to play off that. If Dwayne is busy doing, you know, what are they doing. One of them even said that like, “What am I gonna do?” You know?
